lessonTitle: Architecture Abstraction — The Four Levels
scenario: GlobalTech is in Phase C of the ADM for the Dynamics 365 migration. The Data Architecture team is about to begin modelling the data layer. A junior architect on the team says: "I've started defining the Azure SQL database schema for Dynamics 365 — I figured we'd begin at the Physical level since we already know the target platform is Azure. It'll be faster than going through conceptual and logical levels first."

options.text: Agree with the junior architect. Since Azure is already confirmed as the platform, starting at the Physical level is an efficient use of time and consistent with the ADM's flexibility. Wrong — ADM flexibility applies to phase sequencing, not to skipping abstraction levels within a phase. Starting at Physical without Conceptual or Logical means the data model is driven by the platform's constraints rather than the business's requirements.
options.action: Agree with the junior architect. Since Azure is already confirmed as the platform, starting at the Physical level is an efficient use of time and consistent with the ADM's flexibility.
options.rationale: Wrong — ADM flexibility applies to phase sequencing, not to skipping abstraction levels within a phase. Starting at Physical without Conceptual or Logical means the data model is driven by the platform's constraints rather than the business's requirements.

options.text: Disagree. The junior architect should begin at the Logical level before moving to the Physical level, since the Logical level is implementation-independent. Partially right in identifying the need for a Logical level, but skips the Conceptual level entirely — without first defining the business data entities (what "Customer," "Invoice," "Employee" mean to GlobalTech), the Logical data model will be incomplete.
options.action: Disagree. The junior architect should begin at the Logical level before moving to the Physical level, since the Logical level is implementation-independent.
options.rationale: Partially right in identifying the need for a Logical level, but skips the Conceptual level entirely — without first defining the business data entities (what "Customer," "Invoice," "Employee" mean to GlobalTech), the Logical data model will be incomplete.

options.text: Disagree. The correct approach is to work through the abstraction levels in sequence: Contextual (why this data matters — what business goals and drivers it supports), Conceptual (what data entities the business needs — "Customer," "Invoice," "Absence Record"), Logical (how those entities are structured and related, implementation-independent), then Physical (how they are implemented in Azure SQL). Starting at the Physical level means the data schema will be shaped by what Azure SQL makes easy, rather than what GlobalTech's business processes require. The result is a data model that is technically functional but architecturally misaligned — and expensive to fix once data is migrated. Best answer.
options.action: Disagree. The correct approach is to work through the abstraction levels in sequence: Contextual (why this data matters — what business goals and drivers it supports), Conceptual (what data entities the business needs — "Customer," "Invoice," "Absence Record"), Logical (how those entities are structured and related, implementation-independent), then Physical (how they are implemented in Azure SQL).
options.rationale: Starting at the Physical level means the data schema will be shaped by what Azure SQL makes easy, rather than what GlobalTech's business processes require. The result is a data model that is technically functional but architecturally misaligned — and expensive to fix once data is migrated. Best answer.

options.text: Disagree. The junior architect should first complete the Data Entity model (the conceptual level) to ensure all business data concepts are captured before designing the database schema. Correctly identifies the need to start at the Conceptual level. Loses marks for not mentioning the Logical level between Conceptual and Physical, and for not explaining why the sequence matters architecturally.
